name: Fresenius Medical Care AG
moat_justification: World's leading dialysis provider (about 3,513 clinics, about 290,000 patients, 20-F Item 4.B) with vertical integration into machines/dialyzers (Care Enablement) and unmatched clinic scale — but a reimbursement price-taker in a DaVita duopoly, with ROIC proxy down from 13.6% (2018) to 4.6% (2023/24) recovering to 7.2% (2025) and gross margin down from 33.9% to 25.6%, so the measured franchise earns around its cost of capital, not well above it.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency EUR converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x0.5 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-24), Item 9 'The offer and listing' (p. 147): a two-for-one split of the outstanding ADSs effective December 3, 2012 'changed the ratio of our ADSs to shares from one ADS representing one share to two ADSs representing one share' — so one ADS represents one-half of an ordinary share (depositary: Bank of New York Mellon); the same 1/2 ratio is carried in the NYSE-registered ADS class title) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already

SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (estimate: Anchor 1 (band): last engine-filed SBC value, FY2019 AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments EUR 1,992,000 (statements.json; filed FY2015-2019 range EUR 1,992,000-46,811,000) — EUR 10,000,000 is 5.02x that anchor, inside the 0.1x-10x band. Anchor 2 (filing economics): FY2025 Form 20-F Note 23 'Share-based plans' compensation-expense table — the EQUITY-settled allocations total EUR 8,371,000 in FY2025 (LTIP 2025+ EUR 6,293,000 + MB LTIP 2024+ EUR 2,078,000) and nil in FY2024/FY2023, so EUR 10M is that filing figure rounded up, applied flat); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Fresenius Medical Care consolidated statements of cash flows, investing activities: 'Purchases of property, plant and equipment and capitalized development costs' EUR 915M for FY2025 (Q4/FY2025 financial tables, February 24, 2026, reproducing the FY2025 Form 20-F cash-flow statement filed 2026-02-24); the same line is EUR 699M for FY2024 and EUR 685M for FY2023); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:shares — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-24), Note 22 'Earnings per share' reconciliation of basic and diluted EPS: 'Weighted average number of shares outstanding' 291,190,575 for FY2025 (293,413,449 for FY2024 and FY2023), 'Potentially dilutive shares' shown as nil in all three years, basic EPS = diluted EPS (EUR 3.36 / 1.83 / 1.70, also identical on the face of the income statement); EDGAR companyfacts carries no diluted weighted-average series for any year (fundamentals.json warning: diluted share count not filed for 2016-2025)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 7.1x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (14.7%) vs bull-case tier A (22.0%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: World's largest dialysis provider, moat 5/10 — clears 15% on the conservative override base ($3.23/ADS): weighted IRR 18.1%, IV@15 $27.88 vs $22.17, but the band runs C (bear 14.7%) to A (bull 22.0%) with net debt 3.55x normalized OE on the ADS basis, so size it to the bear end; clears 15% only below $27.88.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: engine output predates release 5.5.0 — re-run the engine before an exit alert; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: World's largest dialysis provider: about 3,513 clinics treating about 290,000 patients (20-F FY2025, Item 4.B) — clinic density and purchasing scale no challenger can replicate quickly
Vertically integrated: Care Enablement makes the machines/dialyzers (incl. the 5008X, first FDA-cleared high-volume hemodiafiltration system in the U.S.) that Care Delivery clinics consume
Life-sustaining, non-discretionary recurring treatments; global dialysis population growing about 4-5%/yr (20-F Item 4.B) on diabetes/hypertension/obesity drivers
Value-Based Care scaling fast (segment revenue +28.2% in FY2025 to EUR 2,247M, segments.json) — a capitated-care position built on the clinic network and nephrologist relationships
moat_against: Reimbursement price-taker: U.S. Medicare/commercial rates are set by payors; FMS does not set its own price for its core treatment

Measured returns do not show a wide moat: ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json) fell from 13.6% in 2018 to 4.6% in 2023 and 2024, recovering only to 7.2% in 2025; gross margin fell from 33.9% (2016) to 25.6% (2025)
U.S. same-market treatment growth was -0.9% in Q2 2026 — the core volume engine is flat, growth is rate/mix and Value-Based Care, not treatments

DaVita duopoly competition in the U.S. and labor-cost pressure across the clinic network; recurring special items (FME25+ program, portfolio optimization, China exit charge of about EUR 110M expected Q3 2026)
